## 2. Declared SSH Hamiltonian and stability

The bath is an infinite alternating weighted graph Laplacian with onsite energy 3, intra-cell hopping \(-2\), inter-cell hopping \(-1\), and Bloch energies

\[
 \lambda_\pm(k)=3\pm e(k),\qquad e(k)=\sqrt{5+4\cos k},\quad -\pi\le k<\pi.
\]

Its absolutely continuous bands are \([0,2]\cup[4,6]\), so it is **gapless at zero** and has a one-photon gap around energy 3. Two hard-core memories \(L,R\) couple to the adjacent normalized gradients \(v_j=(|A_j\rangle-|B_j\rangle)/\sqrt2\). The number-conserving Hamiltonian is

\[

 +g\sum_{j=L,R}\bigl(\sigma_j^+a(v_j)+a^*(v_j)\sigma_j^-\bigr).
 \tag{1}
\]

The earlier exact graph-form identity \(\langle v_j,h^{-1}v_k\rangle_{\rm form}=\delta_{jk}/4\) gives harmonic one-body Schur margin \(3+g^2/4\). \[

## ASTRA — Foundational physics continuation

New result: The reciprocal, gapless SSH waveguide supports a controlled two-qubit entangling operation even though its two-excitation memory state lies inside the two-photon continuum.

The central insight is that being embedded in a continuum does not automatically mean an excitation decays on the timescale of the desired operation. Here, the leading emission pathways cancel algebraically.

### 1. Exact dressed-pair cancellation

Consider two hard-core quantum memories \\(L,R\\), with excitation energy near \\(3B\\), coupled to the same infinite SSH bath. Its one-particle spectrum is

\\[ [0,2B]\cup[4B,6B]. \\]

Thus the memory energy \\(3B\\) lies in a gap, but the energy \\(6B\\) of two excited memories lies inside the two-photon continuum.

Let \\(h\\) be the bath Hamiltonian, \\(v_L,v_R\\) its local coupling profiles, and define, in units \\(B=1\\),

\\[ r_j=(h-3)^{-1}v_j. \\]

I constructed a normalized-up-to-dressing two-excitation state

\\[ |\Psi_g\rangle= |LR\rangle -g\left(|R;r_L\rangle+|L;r_R\rangle\right) +g^2a^\dagger(r_L)a^\dagger(r_R)|0\rangle. \\]

For adjacent gradient ports, direct operator algebra gives the exact identity

\\[ \boxed{ \\|(H_g-6)|\Psi_g\rangle\\| =\frac{g^3}{4\sqrt6}. } \\]

There is no second-order residual, even though freely propagating two-photon states exist at the same total energy.

This is stronger than a perturbative cancellation of an individual scattering amplitude: it holds for the complete infinite-volume Hamiltonian, including every bath mode and both photonic bands.

I independently assembled the hard-core two-particle Hamiltonian on a finite SSH ring and verified the corresponding exact residual identity to approximately \\(10^{-15}\\).

## 2. An entangling-gate theorem despite the open two-photon channel

## Accepted mathematical scope

Both workers independently derive that exchange `XX+YY` plus local `ZI,IZ` preserves equality of the two parity-block determinants. CZ violates that closed invariant, even up to global phase. Thus ideal exchange plus phase controls cannot synthesize or arbitrarily approximate this same two-qubit target.

Both also construct an exact CZ once transverse local gates are supplied. In the normalization `H_ex=J(XX+YY)/2`, two partial exchange intervals total `pi/(2|J|)`. With the source's `J_g=g^2/8+O(g^4)`, exchange time is `4pi/g^2[1+O(g^2)]`. The construction worker additionally supplies an ideal zero-duration-local-control optimality argument; no hardware time optimum follows.

The coordinator read both complete arguments and scripts, then replayed unchanged script copies in separate reviewer directories: all **13 audit checks and 12 construction checks pass**. Original worker outputs remain unchanged. This completed internal mathematical review accepts the stated finite-dimensional control conclusions. It does not audit the producer's infinite-volume spectral theorem, acquire physical pulses, or prove a lower bound for the full SSH Hamiltonian. The proposed fourth-order interaction lies outside the exchange-only model.

## Existing knowledge and physical relevance

The determinant distinction is established matchgate theory, not a new Astra theorem: [Jozsa and Miyake](https://arxiv.org/html/0804.4050v2). [Brod and Galvão](https://arxiv.org/html/1106.1863v1) explain related parity-preserving resources with further circuit assumptions; no many-qubit universality claim is inferred for this device.

Absence from a model is not absence from plausible hardware. The relevant [Kim et al. experimental SSH waveguide](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.11.011015) has individual excitation-drive and flux-control lines. That makes broader controls a substantive comparator to investigate, not a capability to assume impossible. It does not establish the controls, error budget or gradient-port geometry of Astra's exact model. Existing [hard-core Green-function machinery](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.043264) also remains prior art; no model-specific priority was established here.
